chapter: Favorite bands, advice and family reflections
title: Cricket on his father's generation
summary: His son says the older musicians escaped reality by partying because they felt they could not overcome their foe.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: ... something I'd like to ask you being that you're younger than Leonard and myself, when you think of a lot of things that your father accomplished, and you are actively involved in the music field and so forth. When you are as young as you are, what do you think? Do you know the point I'm getting at ... what do you think?

Yeah, I don't know. I try to take into account the fact that it is a different time. I try to put myself into the position of someone who came along during that time. A lot of the things that I'm concerned

with and feel strongly about, it wasn't quite so important at that time or if it was, they didn't see any at the end of light/in the tunnel the way we do now. At least we're actively engaged in a struggle, a social and political struggle, against a foe that we know about. We acknowledge as a foe and we know that this is the enemy over got here. We've got to work and do this to overcome it. during didn't Where during that time they did have any real reason to think that they could overcome that foe or even do battle with that foe so I think they engaged mostly in escaping reality to a certain degree. I mean by playing and having a good time, drinking, partying. Then you can forget about the fact that you can't go here or you can't go there or you're not going to make as much money as somebody that has stolen your music. They were exploited. I think they had a good time while they could. And that's just about what it amounted to. I can't think of too much more to add in relation to, you know, what's happening today and what happened then.
